messages:
zoe: Heads up — saw an odd SSE symptom in eu-prod this morning. Console shows connection as UP for ~30s but there are no events sent, then client reconnects and we get a duplicate billing window. Anyone seen the LB insert an idle probe/halfclose that the runtime doesn't surface?

ashwin: Which LB type? gce ILB or the envoy sidecar?

zoe: GCE ILB in front of nginx -> envoy path. Packet traces show a TCP FIN from the ILB at ~28s after idle, but our app logs never show a socket closed event. Console still displays session as connected and streaming bytes accumulate.

kevin: ugh. that's going to mislead SLO dashboards and cost calc. do you have trace ids?

zoe: trace=tr-9f0c, example log excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-20T08:01:23.123Z] sse: stream=abc123 last_out=2026-03-20T08:00:55Z
[2026-03-20T08:01:23.125Z] net: recv FIN from 10.10.5.12:443 (ILB)
# no higher-level close emitted by runtime for ~5s
[2026-03-20T08:01:28.200Z] sse: client reconnect new_stream=abc123-1
```

tim: That smells like the proxy does a TCP-level idle cleanup that the runtime treats as transient socket noise. We currently only flip session -> closed on application-level EOF. We should detect halfclose and immediately mark session closed for console/metrics.

ashwin: If we mark closed earlier we avoid overcounting tokens, but risk flip-flopping if the client legitimately reconnects and resumes (resume path relies on sticky session). Need to ensure resume idempotency in the face of this.

kevin: Two orthogonal asks: (1) telemetry/alerting — emit a "sse_tcp_halfclose" counter and tag with upstream-proxy and route so we can correlate; (2) UX — console should show "stalled (tcp-halfclose)" instead of connected while we investigate.

eng-console-bot: Created console ticket CN-1427: https://redwood.example.com/console/tickets/CN-1427 (zoe assigned)

zoe: I started a tiny patch to detect net FIN and set session state->closed_for_console immediately (not affecting server resume logic yet). Draft: https://gh.redwood.dev/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/2043

tim: Can you add a metric with histogram of time-between-tcpfin-and-app-ack? That will show how often we fail to surface the event.

zoe: will do. quick snippet I'm testing: 
```
if (tcp_event == FIN) {
  emit_metric("sse_tcp_halfclose", 1, {route, lb_kind});
  mark_console_state(session, "stale_tcp_halfclose");
  // still keep resume token valid for N seconds
}
```

ashwin: Keep resume path unchanged for now. If we start expiring resume tokens earlier we'll break sticky clients on flaky networks. For rollout, prefer feature-flagged console-only visibility first.

kevin: Agreed. Feature flag for console/state-only change. After 1 week of telemetry we can consider affecting routing decision (failover vs keep trying).

zoe: Note: billing pipeline reads token emission based on session windows. Might need a guard in billing to not attribute token accrual to stale_tcp_halfclose windows — I'll open a billing issue.

deploy-bot: canary deploy initiated for runtime/patch-2043 to cluster eu-canary at 2026-03-20T12:15:00Z

tim: If canary looks good, console change + metric emitted is low risk. We should also add a dashboard tile: "SSE half-close events by upstream" and an alert if rate > 0.5% of open sessions.

kevin: Also add an annotation in routing docs about ILB aggressive idle-timeouts and the recommended proxy config (tcp_keepalive vs application ping). Link: https://docs.redwood.dev/platform/proxy-idle-tuning

zoe: Action items I have: add metric + console-only state change behind feature flag (PR up), open billing ticket, add dashboard tile. Will post canary results.

ashwin: sgtm. tag me on the PR for telemetry labels (route/tenant).

kevin: Thanks all. If anyone sees token accrual spikes correlated with these traces, @kevin please paste here.

zoe: canary successful on eu-canary (no regression) — metrics show ~12 halfclose events last hour concentrated on cluster a. Dashboard tile added to staging.

tim: Nice. Let's keep console-only for 7d then reassess whether routing should treat tcp halfclose as terminal for session placement.

kevin: filing follow-up RFC to decide routing semantics: sticky-resume vs immediate-failover when tcp halfclose detected. RFC id RFC-7802

zoe: thanks, closing CN-1427 once billing ticket created.

eng-console-bot: CN-1427 updated: bill-ticket=BL-558 (zoe), canary=pass, slate=staged
